Writ Petition Nos. 4012 and 2876 of 1999 
With Writ Petition No. 1948 of 2000 and Writ Petition No. 2305 of 2002
lawyer:

Awsafur Rahman, Advocate—For Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 
Abdul Wadid Bhuiyan with SRM Lutfor Rahman, Advocate—For Respondent No. 3 (Md Khademul Islam).

Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan and Syed Mokaddas Ali with SRM Lutfor Rahman, Advocate—For Respondents 5 and 8 Md Khademul Islam and Md Khalilur Rahman. 
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Advocate—For the Petitioner.

parties:
Mohammad Ali ------ Petitioner and others
Vs.
Bangladesh Standard and Testing Institution (BSTI) and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Joynul Abedin, J : Since the Rules involve common questions of fact and law between the same parties, they are accordingly heard and disposed of by the single judgment.

2. In Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999, Rule nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned orders as contained in letter No. BSTI/Admn/77/98/ (Part) 3023 dated 31-5-99 Annexure-U, and letter No BSTI/Admn-7/88/1553 dated 31-3-98, Annexure-M(2), passed by the respondents Nos. 1 and 2 promoting the respondent Nos. 3-5 superseding the petitioner and regularising the previous service of the respondent No. 3 in the development project of the Bangladesh Standard and Testing Institution (BSTI) by a bridge in spite of break of service should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

3. The case of the petitioner is that he passed BSc (Hons) in Physics and MSc in Physics from the Rajshahi University in 1980 and 1982 respectively and secured 2nd class. He was first appointed as an Examiner (Electrical) in Bangladesh Standard Institution (BSI) by a letter of appointment No. BDSI/Pro-89/70(Part) dated 22-5-83. Subsequently, the petitioner was appointed as Inspector (Meteorology) in BSI vide letter of appointment No. BDSI/Pro-89/7(Part) dated 24-11-83, Annexure-B to the writ petition, and he joined the service of BSI in the said post on 28-11-83. The respondent No. 3, Md Khademul Islam, was appointed as Inspector (Meteorology) in the development project of the BSI on the same date and he joined the service on 28-11-83. Respondent No. 4, Shawkat Osman, and respondent No. 5, ABM Mortuza Hussain, were also appointed as Inspector (Meteorology) in BSI on 8-12-83 and 15-12-83 respectively.

4. The petitioner in recognition of his efficiency and meritorious service was promoted to the post of Senior Examiner, Class I, (Grade IX) of the modified new scale of pay, 1985 in BSTI with effect from 4-9-88, Annexure-C to the writ petition. In 1989 the petitioner was chosen to attend the training course in Meteorology Liner Management Technicians/Industrial Measurement Technics Programme held in West Germany for a period of one year from 2-10-89 to 30-9-90 and his entire period in training abroad was to be treated as on duty vide office memo dated 21-8-91, Annexure-D to the writ petition.

5. While the petitioner was undergoing the aforesaid training in West Germany, respondent Nos. 4 and 5 were promoted to the post of Assistant Director (Meteorology) in the meeting held by the Selection Board on 9-7-90 and, in fact, there was no viva-voce examination. In the same meeting it was decided that the vacancy in the post of Assistant Director would be kept open for the petitioner subject to an interview on his return, Annexure-6 to the affidavit-in-reply filed by the petitioner. The petitioner after his return from West Germany made various representations to the respondent No. 1 to consider his case of promotion. The petitioner also drew the attention of the respondent No. 1 to the fact that there was already a precedent created in this regard by promoting some officers during their training aboard on the basis of seniority and merit but without any success. Respondent Nos. 4 and 5, who were appointed to the post of Assistant Director as per the decision taken in the meeting held by the Selection Board on 9-7-90, were junior to the petitioner as they were appointed as Inspector (Meteorology) on 8-12-83 and 15-12-83 respectively and the petitioner was appointed as Inspector (Meteorology) on 24-11-83.

6. After the return of the petitioner from his training aboard he was promoted as Assistant Director (Meteorology) in the same scale and grade as Senior Examiner on 29-3-92, Annexure-E to the writ petition. He was later transferred to the post of Senior Examiner on 30-5-94 with the same scale as that of Assistant Director, Annexure-F to the writ petition, on the plea that he was temporarily promoted as Assistant Director although it was not so mentioned in the letter of promotion dated 29-3-92, Annexure-E to the writ petition. The selection committee thereafter promoted the petitioner as Assistant Director on 14-8-97, Annexure-G to the writ petition, stating that the petitioner was in current charge of the post of an Assistant Director before although it was not so. The petitioner was awarded selection grade scale VII with retrospective effect from 10-1-94 by office order dated 31-12-97, Annexure-I to the writ petition. The respondent Nos. 4 and 5 were also given selection grade and they were placed at serials 21 and 22 respectively, Annexure-I to the writ petition. The respondent No. 3 was however not given the selection grade as he was in the development project of the BSTI and not in the revenue budget of the BSTI. Since the project in which the respondent No. 3 was appointed as an Assistant Director on 16+11-88 came to an end his service was terminated on 28-3-94 with effect from 31-3-94, Annexure-K to the writ petition. Thereafter, the respondent No. 3 applied for the post of Assistant Director in the BSTI afresh pursuant to an advertisement in that regard on 17-7-94 and he was thus appointed as the Assistant Director in the BSTI afresh on 9-10-94 after he was out of service for more than 6 months, Annexure-L-1 to the writ petition.

7. In 1992, the BSTI prepared a provisional seniority list and circulated the same on 6-7-92 wherein the petitioner was placed at serial No. 19 while the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 were respectively placed at serial Nos. 12 and 14. Since respondent No. 3 was in the development project of the BSTI he was not placed in the said seniority list. The petitioner raised objection to his placement in the provisional seniority list below the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 and prayed for correction by fixing his seniority over the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 but without any success. Subsequently a combined seniority list was prepared by office order dated 25-10-98, but this time too the petitioner was not only placed below the respondents Nos. 4 and 5 but he was even placed below the respondent No. 3. The petitioner, therefore, raised objection for being placed below the respondent Nos. 3-5 as he was senior to them in service. While the petitioner was continuing in making the representations for placing him below the respondent Nos. 3-5 in the combined seniority list, BSTI on 31-5-99 promoted the respondent Nos. 3-5 to the post of Deputy Director by superseding the petitioner by the impugned office order dated 31-5-99, Annexure-U to the writ petition. The BSTI in order to facilitate the promotion of the respondent No. 3 to the post of Deputy Director bridged up, the gap of his service for about more than 6 months for not being in the service of either in the project of BSTI or in the BSTI itself.

8. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2, namely, the BSTI, appeared and contested the Rule by filing the affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the petitioner was appointed temporarily as an Inspector (Meteorology) under a development project of the BSTI namely, "Implementation of Metric System and Strengthening of Bangladesh Standard Institution" on 28-11-83 and not in the BSTI itself. Since his service as Inspector in the BSTI was not regularised before 29-7-97, his promotion from the post of Inspector to Senior Examiner on 4-9-88 was illegal. Accordingly, the promotion of the petitioner to the post of Assistant Director (Meteorology) by office Memo dated 29-3-92 was irregular and it was therefore subsequently cancelled by transferring the petitioner to his former lower post of Senior Examiner by office Memo dated 30-5-95. Later the petitioner got regular promotion to the post of Assistant Director (Meteorology) on 14-8-97. But even that promotion was illegal as he did not serve the minimum requisite period for 3 years as Senior Examiner after regularisation of his service on 29-7-97 as Inspector. The petitioner therefore acquired eligibility for promotion to the post of Assistant Director on 28-7-2000 and not before that date. Accordingly, the petitioner was not eligible for selection grade scale and the selection grade given to the petitioner by Memo dated 31-12-97 was illegal.

9. It is further contended by the BSTI (respondent Nos. 1 and 2) that the respondent No. 3 was first appointed on 28-11-83 as Inspector (Meteorology) in a project under the development budget of the BSTI like the petitioner. Respondent No. 3 later applied for the post of Assistant Director in another project under the development budget of the BSTI pursuant to an advertisement and was appointed as an Assistant Director on 16-11-88. The tenure of the project ended on 31-3-94. Accordingly, the service of the respondent No. 3 was terminated on that date. Subsequently, the post of Assistant Director in the development project was transferred to the revenue budget of BSTI and the respondent No. 3 was appointed to the said post on 9-10-94 after having been selected in open competition with others. The termination of service of the respondent No. 3 in the project as Assistant Director with the end of the project was illegal as he ought to have been allowed to be retained in service till he was appointed as HC-16 Assistant Director on 9-10-94 in the Revenue budget of the BSTI. The respondent No. 3 therefore, submitted an application to the authority on 6-11-97 for bridging up the gap in the service for about 6 months between the date of termination of his service in the project on 28-3-94 and the date of his regular appointment in the same post as Assistant Director on 9-10-94 in the revenue budget of BSTI. BSTI thereupon, by office order dated 31-3-98 bridged up the said gap and therefore there was continuity of his service. Respondent No. 3 was accordingly, promoted to the post of Deputy Director before the petitioner by the impugned office order dated 31-5-99. It is further contended by the BSTI that the respondents Nos. 4 and 5 were appointed as Inspector (Meteorology) and because of their satisfactory service record they were promoted to the post of Assistant Director and Deputy Director on recommendation of the Selection Committee.

10. The respondent Nos. 3 and 5 also appeared and contested the Rule by filing separate affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegations contained in the writ petition. The case of the respondent No. 3 is that the petitioners as well as respondent Nos. 3, 4 and 5 were all appointed as Inspector (Meteorology) in the development project of the BSTI known as "Introduction of Metric Systems of Weights and Measurement in the Country and Strengthening of Bangladesh Standard and Testing Institution." The petitioner was appointed on 28-11-83, respondent No. 3 was also appointed on the same date ie 28-11-83, and respondent Nos. 4 and 5 were appointed on 8-12-83 and 15-12-83 respectively. When the respondent No. 3 was serving in the post of Inspector (Meteorology), BSTI advertised for filling up the post of Assistant Director. Respondent No. 3 then resigned from his post as Inspector and applied for the post of Assistant Director in the project afresh. He was thus appointed as Assistant Director in the project on 16-11-88and thereafter he served as Assistant Director in the project from 16-11-88 to 31-3-94. Thereafter, the respondent No. 3 secured his appointment as Assistant Director in the Revenue Budget of BSTI on 9-10-94 through an open competition with others pursuant to the advertisement made in this regard by the BSTI. Since the petitioner and the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 did not make any application for appointment to the post of Assistant Director in the Revenue Budget of the BSTI pursuant to the advertisement made on 17-7-94 the promotion of the petitioner as well as the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 to the post of Assistant Director in the BSTI in 1992 and 1990 respectively was neither regular nor legal inasmuch as they were not entitled to be promoted to the post of Assistant Director in the BSTI before the post of Inspector in the BSTI was regularised after the said post of Inspector was transferred in the revenue budget of the BSTI. Accordingly, the respondent No. 3 was senior to the petitioner as well as to respondent Nos. 4 and 5 as Assistant Director in the BSTI. It is also the case of the respondent No. 3 that the post of Assistant Director in the development project of BSTI was transferred to the revenue budget of BSTI vide Government Order No. Shim/Sha /89 dated 27-6-94. The process of transferring this post from the development budget to the revenue budget of BSTI took time and meanwhile the project ended on 31-3-94. Accordingly, the service of the respondent No. 3 as Assistant Director in the project was terminated and this termination of his service was illegal and violative of the Government Circular dated 11-1-92. Hence, the respondent No. 3 submitted an application on 16-11-97 to the concerned authority for bridging up the gap of service for more than 6 months with effect from the date of termination of his service on 28-3-94 till his regular appointment as Assistant Director on 9-10-94 in the Revenue Budget of the BSTI. The BSTI then bridged up the gap in his service by office order No.BSTI/Admn/ 74/88 /9553 /dated 31-3-98. In this view of the matter, the service of the respondent No. 3 as Assistant Director in the revenue budget of the BSTI was and still is liable to be counted from 16-11-88 i.e. from the date the respondent No. 3 joined the post of Assistant Director in the project of the BSTI. Hence, the promotion of the respondent No. 3 to the post of Deputy Director (Meteorology) by the impugned office Memo dated 31-5-99 was legal and in accordance with the provision of BSTI Service Regulations, 1989.

11. Further case of the respondent No. 3 with regard to the selection grade of the petitioner is that one is required to be a permanent class I officer in order to become eligible for the selection grade of Taka 4100/= - 6500/=. Since the petitioner was not regularised in the post of Inspector in the revenue budget of the BSTI until 29-7-97 he was not eligible for selection grade scale. Hence, the selection grade given to the petitioner was illegal and without lawful authority.

12. Respondent No. 4 did not appear and contest the Rule. The respondent No. 5 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegations made in the writ petition. The case of the respondent No. 5 is that he was promoted to the post of Assistant Director (Meteorology) with effect from 2-10-90 on the basis of the system of promotion prevailing in the BSTI and in accordance with the provision of regulation 7 read with regulation 14 of the BSTI Service Regulations, 1989. Therefore, there was no question of superseding the petitioner nor there was any violation of any procedure connected with the promotion of respondent No. 5 by the BSTI. Accordingly, the respondent No. 5 was rightly placed at serial No. 12 in the provisional seniority list as Assistant Director (Meteorology). Similarly, the respondent No. 5 was also rightly placed at serial No. 26 above the position of the petitioner in the combined seniority list in view of the fact that he was promoted to the post of Assistant Director earlier than the petitioner. In the circumstances, the promotion of the respondent No. 5 to the post of Deputy Director (Meteorology) by the impugned order dated 31-5-99 is rightly given and is not liable to be interfered.

13. In Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999, Rule nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order as contained in letters No. BSTI/Admn-17/ 90(part)/3024 and BSTI/Admn/17/93 (part) 3023, both dated 31-5-99, Annexures-MI and M2 to the writ petition, and memo No. BSTI/Admn-17/93(Part)1633 dated 21-4-1998, Annexure-M to the writ petition, issued by the respondents Nos. 3 and 4 promoting the respondent Nos. 5-8 to the post of Deputy Director superseding the petitioner and amending the petitioner's approved selection grade scale dated 31-12-97 should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and why the respondent No. 2 should not be directed to promote the petitioner to the post of Deputy Director as the petitioner is senior to the respondents Nos. 5-8.

14. The case of the petitioner is that he passed Diploma-in-Mechanical Engineering in 1982. He was appointed as Senior Examiner (Measure) in Bangladesh Standard Institution (BSI) which was subsequently known as BSTI by the letter of appointment dated 22-5-83. He was thereafter promoted to the post of Assistant Director by office Memo dated 22-1-91. The respondent No. 5, Md Khademul Islam, on the other hand, was appointed as Inspector in the development project of BSI on 28-11-83 and he worked as such till 15-11-88. Thereafter, respondent No. 5 joined as Assistant Director (Meteorology) in another development project of BSTI and at the end of the project the concerned authority cancelled the appointment of respondent No. 5 on 28-3-94. Subsequently, respondent No. 5 was given appointment as an Assistant Director (Meteorology) in the revenue budget of the BSTI on 9-10-94 after he was out of service for about more than 6 (six) months from 28-3-94 to 9-10-94. Thereafter, his aforesaid gap of service of more than 6 month was illegally bridged up in violation of section 3B of the Employees Transferred from Development Project to the Post of Revenue Budget Regularisation and Seniority Fixation Rules, 1995 and thereafter he was promoted to the post of Deputy Director (Meteorology) on 31-5-1999 superseding the petitioner in violation of the Service Regulations, 1989, although the petitioner was senior to respondent No. 5 by more than 3 years.

15. Further case of the petitioner is that respondent No. 6 was appointed as Inspector (Meteorology) in BSI violating the terms and conditions of appointment as per the advertisement dated 8-9-83 published in the daily Bangladesh Observer in that the respondent No. 6 was under-aged, being 20 years at the time of appointment, and the requisite age for the post was 23 to 30 years. Moreover, respondent Nos. 6 and 7 were given promotion to the post of Assistant Director by office order date 8-10-90 in violation of the BSTI Service Regulations 1989 as their seniority and ACR were not taken into account while giving them promotion by resorting to pick and choose policy.

16. It is also the case of the petitioner that the respondent No. 8 was appointed as Co-ordination Officer in the BSTI on ad hoc basis on 23-4-90. Although Rule 5 of the Regularisation of Ad hoc Employees Appointment Rules, 1994 provides that a seniority of an incumbent shall be determined from the date of regularisation of his ad-hoc appointment the seniority of respondent No. 8 was determined not from the date of regularisation of his service but from the date of his ad hoc appointment on 28-4-90 in violation of the aforesaid Rules. Accordingly, the Audit Report dated 16-5-99 of the BSTI took exception and pointed out this irregularity. In this background of the matter, BSTI illegally prepared a combined seniority list of its officers and employees and placed the petitioner below the respondent Nos. 6, 7 and 8. Accordingly, the petitioner made various representations for correction of the aforesaid combined seniority list but without any success.

17. The BSTI, however, in consideration of the brilliant service career and excellent ACR of the petitioner as Assistant Director (Meteorology) accorded him a selection grade scale of Taka 4100/= - 7100/= with effect from 6-5-95. The BSTI subsequently on 21-4-98 most arbitrarily amended the date of the petitioner's selection grade scale and gave the same date of selection grade to the respondent No. 8 from 6-5-95 and the petitioner's date of selection grade scale was given from 26-2-98 which was initially given to respondent No. 8. Although the petitioner is senior to the respondent Nos. 5-8, BSTI illegally and with mala fide intention amended the date of petitioner's approved selection grade scale and promoted the respondent Nos. 5-8 to the post of Deputy Director with effect from 31-5-99 superseding the petitioner in violation of the BSTI Service Regulations, 1989 and its schedule. The petitioner accordingly, made various representations against the aforesaid promotion and the undue amendment of the date of his approved selection grade scale but received no response from the BSTI, hence the present writ petition.

18. In Writ Petition Nos. 1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2003 Md Khademul Islam, (respondent No. 3 in Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999 and respondent No. 5 in Writ Petition No. 2876 is the petitioner. Rule nisi was issued at his instance in Writ Petition No. 1948 of 2000 calling upon the respondents to show cause why the impugned decision as contained in memo No. BSTI (Admn)1-166-94-498(5) dated 29-7-97, Annexure-U to the writ petition, insofar as it relates to regularisation of service of the respondent Nos. 6 and 7, Md Abu Hussain and Mohammad Ali, in the post of Inspector with retrospective effect from 1-7-86 and the memo No. BSTI (Admn) 17/93(Part) 1/2070 dated 31-12-97, Annexure-Q to the writ petition, insofar as it relates to giving selection grade to respondent Nos. 6 and 7 with effect from 6-5-95, and placement of respondent Nos. 6 and 7 at Serial Nos. 28 and 38 respectively in the combined seniority list as Assistant Director as circulated under the Memo No. BSTI Admn/396 /98 /582(6) dated 25-10-98, Annexure-Q to the writ petition, should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and are of no legal effect and why the respondent No. 2 should not be directed to cancel the impugned memos dated 29-7-97 and 31-12-97, Annexure U and Q. It may be mentioned here that respondents Nos. 6 and 7, Md Abu Hossain and Mohammad Ali, in Writ Petition No. 1948 of 2000 against whom the present Rule is obtained are petitioners in the aforesaid Writ Petition Nos. 2876 of 1999 and 4012 of 1999 respectively.

19. In Writ Petition 2305 of 2002 Md Khademul Islam, petitioner in the preceding Writ Petition No. 1948 of 2000, is also the petitioner and Rule nisi was issued at his instance calling upon the respondents 1-5 to show cause as to why the order contained in the office Memo No. BSTI/Admn-17/90/1873 dated 22-1-1991, Annexure-J-1 to the writ petition, issued under the signature of the Director General of BSTI promoting the respondent No. 5, Md Abu Hossain, petitioner in Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999, to the post of Assistant Director (Meteorology) in BSTI should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

20. The case of the petitioner both in Writ Petition 1948 of 2000 and Writ Petition No. 2305 of 2002 is that the he was appointed as Inspector (Meteorology) on 28-11-93 in a development project of the BSTI known as "Introduction of Metric System and Strengthening of Bangladesh Standard and Testing Institution". He was thereafter appointed as Assistant Director (Meteorology) on 16-11-88 in another development project known as "Establishment and Strengthening of Bangladesh Standard and Testing Institution." After the transfer of the post of Assistant Director from the development project to the revenue budget of the BSTI the said post of Assistant Director was advertised. The petitioner then applied for and was appointed as Assistant Director in the revenue budget of the BSTI on 9-10-94 on regular basis but after the end of the project on 30-6-94 the service of the petitioner in the project as Assistant Director was terminated on 28-6-94. Accordingly, the petitioner Md Khademul Islam submitted application on 6-11-97 to the authority for bridging up the gap of service for about 6 months from the date of termination of his service in the project to the date of his regular appointment to the post of Assistant Director in the revenue judge of the BSTI. The BSTI allowed his application and bridged up the said gap /break up in service and subsequently promoted him to the post of Deputy Director (Meteorology) on recommendation of the selection board on 31-5-99.

21. We have heard Mrs Sigma Huda, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan for respondent No. 3, Mr Sheikh Awsafur Rahman for the BSTI and Mr Serajul Hoque for respondent No. 5. We have heard Mr Shafique Ahmed appearing for the petitioner in Writ Petition 2876 of 1999, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan for respondent Nos. 5 and 8 and Mr Sheikh Awsafur Rahman for BSTI and in Writ Petition Nos. 1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2002 Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan for the petitioner, Mr Awsafur Rahman for BSTI and Mr Shafique Ahmed for respondent No. 5.

22. It is argued for the petitioners in Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999 and 2876 of 1999 that the petitioners got their appointment as Inspector and senior examiner respectively in 1983 in the revenue budget of the BSTI and not in the development project of the BSTI Md Khademul Islam, respondent No. 3 in Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999 and respondent No. 5 in Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999, was appointed firstly as Inspector (Meteorology) one development project of the BSTI and thereafter as Assistant Director on 16-11-88 in another development project of the BSTI. After the project ended on 30-6-94 service of Md Khademul Islam in the project was terminated and he was out of service for more than 6 months. After the post of Assistant Director (Meteorology) in the project was transferred to the revenue budget of the BSTI advertisement was made by the BSTI for recruitment in the said post of Assistant Director. Md Khademul Islam then applied for the said post and he was eventually appointed as Assistant Director (Meteorology) in the revenue budget of the BSTI on 9-10-94 afresh. Although there was break of service of Md Khademul Islam for more than 6 months, BSTI, it is submitted, illegally bridged up the gap of service of Md Khademul Islam on 31-3-98 in violation of Rule 3(kha) of the Employees Transferred from Development Budget to Revenue Budget and Seniority Fixation Rules, 1995. Respondent Khademul Islam was therefore illegally considered senior to the petitioner Mohammad Ali in Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999 and the petitioner Md Abu Hossain in Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999. It is also argued that the claim of the BSTI and Md Khademul Islam that both the petitioner Mohammad Ali in Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999 and Md Abu Hossain in Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999 were appointed in the development budget of the BSTI like Md Khademul Islam is not tenable being incorrect as this position is not supported by their respective appointment letters. The said writ petitioners were for the first time informed on 29-7-97 by BSTI after 14 years of their service that they were appointed in the development project in 1983 as Inspector (Meteorology) and their services were regularised on 29-7-97 with effect from 1-7-86. It is also argued that the respondents Md Khademul Islam, Md Shawkat Osman and ABM Mortuza Hossain and Md Khalilur Rahman are juniors to the said writ petitioners Mohammad Ali and Md Abu Hossain in service and, as such, their promotion to the post of Deputy Director superseding the petitioners Mohammad Ali and Md Abu Hossain is illegal and without jurisdiction.

23. We have examined the respective appointment letters of the said writ petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md Abu Hossain, and we do not find any word or expression in their appointment letters even to suspect that they were not appointed in the revenue budget but in the development budget of the BSTI. Except Md Khademul Islam, who is respondent in Writ Petition No. 4015 of 1999 and Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999 and petitioner in Writ Petition Nos. 1948 of 2000 and 2035 of 2002, all the other petitioners and respondents were appointed in the revenue budget of BSTI.

<u>24. In this regard, it is worthwhile to mention and refer to the report of the Parliamentary Sub-Committee, Annexure-5 to the affidavit-in-opposition, filed by respondent Khademul Islam and Md Khalilur Rahman in Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999, that even the Director General of BSTI had admitted before this committee that although the aforesaid petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Abu Hossain, were appointed in the project of the BSTI but this was not mentioned either in the advertisement made for those posts nor in the appointment letters of these two petitioners. It is therefore, clear that the petitioners were neither aware nor they were informed before 29-7-97 that they were not appointed in the revenue budget of the BSTI but in the development project of the BSTI. Since the petitioners had no knowledge nor it was made known to them until about 14 years later, it was not permissible in law for the BSTI to regularise their service with retrospective effect that is from 1-7-86 to the detriment and disadvantage of the petitioners. The petitioners, having joined the service of the BSTI in the post of Inspector (Meteorology) in 1983 and also having enjoyed all the rights and privileges attached to the service, have acquired a vested interest to have their seniority counted from the date of their appointment in 1983 and not from 1-7-86 purportedly shown as the date of regularisation of service. Such regularisation of service is palpably illegal and without jurisdiction inasmuch as it is done at such a belated stage nearly 14 years of their appointment and that too in violation of the natural justice.</u>

<u>25. We have noted from the record that respondent Khademul Islam was initially appointed as Inspector and thereafter as Assistant Director in the project of the BSTI. This position is very clear not only from the advertisement made in this regard but also from his appointment letters. It is also very clear that on the conclusion of the project on 30-3-94 service of Md Khademul Islam in the project as Assistant Director was terminated and he was out of service for more than 6 months. Subsequently, an advertisement for the post of Assistant Director in the revenue budget of the BSTI was made and Md Khademul Islam applied for it along with others and he was appointed afresh as an Assistant Director (Meteorology) in the revenue budget of the BSTI on 9-10-94. This appointment of respondent Khademul Islam as an Assistant Director (Meteorology) in the revenue budget of the BSTI was a fresh appointment and thus the continuity of his service for more than 6 months from 28-3-94 to 9-10-94. The bridging up of this gap in service, in our opinion, is illegal as it is not authorised or supported by any law. Rather in view of Rule 3 (Kha) of the Employees Transferred from Development 'Project to the Post of Revenue Budget Regularisation and Seniority Fixation Rules, 1995, Annexure-E to Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999, because of the gap of service for more that 6 (six) months, it was not even permissible for BSTI to regularise the service of respondent Khademul Islam, far less to bridge up the said gap. Hence the impugned order bridging up of the service gap of Khademul Islam as contained in letter dated 31-3-98 vide Annexure-M(2) to Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999 is declared illegal and without jurisdiction and is accordingly, set aside. Relevant portion of Rule 3 is reproduced below:</u>

<u>"৩/নিয়মিত- করন পদ্ধতি-প্রকল্পের কোনো কর্মকর্তা বা কর্মচারীকে নিম্নবর্ণিত শর্তে নিয়মিত করা যাইবে-</u>

<u>(খ) নিয়মিত-করণের তারিখ পর্যন্ত পূর্বের চাকুরীর ধারাবাহিকতা বজায় থাকিতে হইবে ;..............."</u>

<u>26. Petitioner Mohammad Ali was appointed as Assistant Director (Meteorology) by way of promotion on 29-3-1992 vide Annexure-'E' to the Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999. Petitioner Md Abu Hossain was appointed as Assistant Director on promotion on 20-1-1991 vide Annexure-'B' to the Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999. In this view of the matter, it is palpably clear that respondent Khademul Islam was junior to both the petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Abu Hossain, in the service not only as Inspector but also as Assistant Director (Meteorology). Therefore, the promotion of respondent Khademul Islam to the post of Deputy Director (Meteorology) in the BSTI on 31-5-99 without considering the case of the above petitioners for promotion is palpably illegal and without jurisdiction.</u>

<u>27. Similarly, we find that respondents Nos. 4 and 5, Md Shawkat Osman and ABM Mortaza Hossain Shah, are also junior to both the petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Abu Hussain. In spite of this position, respondents Md Shawkat Osman and ABM Mortuza Hossain were promoted as Assistant Director in the BSTI on 8-10-1990 superseding the petitioners Mohammad Ali and Abu Hossain without considering their case for promotion. Hence the promotion of Md Shawkat Osman and Mortuza Hossain on 8-10-1990 was illegal. While the petitioner Mohammad Ali was away to West Germany on a training programme respondents Md Shawkat Osman and Mortuza Hossain were promoted to the post of Assistant Director in BSTI. While giving promotion to respondents Md Shaukat Osman and Mortuza Hossain, concerned authority put it on record that petitioner Mohammad Ali could not be promoted as he was abroad but his case of promotion would be considered on his return from West Germany. But BSTI did not consider the case of promotion of Mohammad Ali on his return. Petitioner Mohammad Ali was entitled to in absentia promotion and his seniority was protected in his promoted position as per the next below rule, as is evident from the Office Memorandum No. MFR (R-II) S-203/83-2(500) dated 1-1-1984 issued by the Ministry of Establishment and Reorganisation, Annexure-P to Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999. As a result, his placement in the combined seniority list, prepared for the Assistant Director, below the respondents Md Khademul Islam, Shawkat Osman and ABM Mortuza Hossain Shah is illegally made. In this view of the matter, the impugned order of promotion dated 31-5-99 of respondents Khademul Islam, Shawkat Osman and ABM Mortuza Hossain in the post of Deputy Director (Meteorology is declared illegal and without jurisdiction and is set aside. Since petitioner Mohammad Ali (WP 4012 of 1999) and petitioner Md Abu Hussain (WP 2876 of 1999) are senior to respondents Khademul Islam, Shawkat Hossain and ABM Mortuza Hossain, BSTI is required in law to consider the case of promotion of the said petitioners to the post of Deputy Director.</u>

<u>28. Since the petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md Abu Hossain, were never informed that they were appointed in the development budget of BSTI and not in the revenue budget of BSTI and since the petitioner Mohammad Ali was promoted to the post of Assistant Director (Meteorology) by the Office Memorandum dated 29-3-1992 of BSTI and petitioner Md Abu Hussain was promoted to the post of Assistant Director (Meteorology) by Office memorandum dated 22-1-1991, their seniority over the said respondents was illegally disturbed and affected on the plea that they were not appointed in the revenue budget but in the development budget of BSTI. Since the petitioners, Mohammad Ali and Md Abu Hussain, were promoted to the post of Assistant Director (Meteorology) with effect from 29-3-1992 and 22-1-1991 respectively in accordance with law and these orders of promotion were acted upon they acquired vested right to retain and continue in their promoted post of Assistant Director and BSTI was debarred in law from interfering or affecting the said promotion in any manner. The cases of Pakistan vs. Himayatullah 21 DLR (SC) 238, 47 DLR (AD) 87 and PLD 1964 SC 503 are referred to in this connection. The aforesaid promotion of Mohammad Ali and Md Abu Hossain as Assistant Director must be considered to be valid and legally exist since BSTI did not set aside the said promotion in accordance with law by giving them any opportunity to show cause. In other words, aforesaid promotion was not liable to be disturbed without compliance with the principle of natural justice.</u>

<u>29. Respondent No. 8, Md Khalilur Rahman, in Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999, was appointed as Co-Ordination Officer on ad-hoc basis on 18-4-1990 in the BSTI vide appointment letter dated 23-4-1990, Annexure-'H' to the Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999. This post was not there in the organogram of the BSTI nor in the BSTI Service Regulations, 1989 at the time when Md Khalilur Rahman was appointed in that post. This post was therefore liable to be governed and regulated by the Regularisation of Ad-hoc Employees Appointment Rules, 1994 of the Ministry of Establishment. Rule 4(1)(Ka) of the said Rules permits regularisation of such ad-hoc appointment provided it (appointment) was made according to the connected rules of appointment of the post. Further, Rule 5(1) of the said Rules provides that the seniority of an ad-hoc appointee is required to be determined from the date of regularisation of the service of such ad-hoc appointee. Respondent Md Khalilur Rahman is not shown to have been appointed on ad-hoc basis according to any service rules. The service of Md Khalilur Rahman therefore, could not be regularised in law. Nonetheless, BSTI regularised the service of Md Khalilur Rahman. But such regularisation cannot be held to be in accordance with law. Despite this, respondent Md Khalilur Rahman was promoted to the post of Deputy Director superseding the petitioners Mohammad Ali and Md Abu Hussain counting his seniority from the date of his ad-hoc appointment in violation of Rules 5(1) of the said Rules, 1994 and not from the date of regularisation of his service. Rule 4(1) is as follows:</u>

<u>"এডহকভিত্তিক নিযুক্ত কর্মচারীগণ নিম্নবর্ণিত শর্ত সাপেক্ষে তাঁদের স্ব স্ব পদে নিয়মিত হইবেন , যথা :-</u>

<u>(ক) এডহকভিত্তিক নিযুক্ত হওয়ার সময়ের সংশ্লিষ্ট পদের প্রচলিত নিয়োগ বিধি বা পদ্ধতি অনুসারে নিযুক্ত হইতে হইবে;........."</u>

<u>Rule 5(1) provides:</u>

<u>“এই বিধিমালার অধীন নিয়মিতকরণকৃত কোনো কর্মচারী জ্যেষ্ঠতা কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক নিয়মিতকরণের তারিখ হইতে গণনা করা হইবে”</u>

<u>30. Moreover, the BSTI most arbitrarily and illegally amended the date of selection grade of the petitioner Md Abu Hossain from 6-5-1995 to 21-4-1998 and the date of selection grade of respondent Khalilur Rahman was amended from 21-4-1998 to 6-5-1995. Audit Department by letter dated 16-5-1999 raised objection against ad-hoc appointment of Md Khalilur Rahman and also against giving selection grade to him stating that his ad-hoc appointment as Co-ordination Officer and giving selection grade to him before 9-11-96 are illegal. This position is clear from Annexure-'J' to Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999. This interchange of the date of the selection grade by amending the rule of selection grade of the petitioner Md Abu Hussain is therefore, declared illegal as it was done without giving him any opportunity to show cause. Because the selection grade initially given to Md Abu Hossain from 6-5-95 was acted upon and accordingly, vested right was created in his favour to retain his selection grade effective from 6-5-95.</u>

<u>31. For the reasons stated above, the Rules in both the Writ Petition No. 4012 of 1999 and Writ Petition No. 2876 of 1999 are made absolute. The Rules in Writ Petition Nos. 1948 of 2000 and 2305 of 2002 by which Md Khademul Islam challenged the regularisation of service of Mohammad Ali and Md Abu Hossain and their placement in the Seniority list are liable to fail for the reasons given above.</u>

To sum-up, the Rules in Writ Petition Nos. 4012 of 1999 and 2876 of 1999 are made absolute and the Rules in Writ Petition No. 1948 of 2000 and Writ Petition No. 2305 of 2002 are hereby discharged without any order as to costs. The BSTI is therefore directed to consider the case of Mohammad Ali and Md Abu Hossain for promotion to the post of Deputy Director without any further delay.

End.
